$comment: GOLDEN VECTORS for the canvas binary wire protocol (contracts/sandbox/canvas-wire.json). Each entry pairs a source frame (canvasId, frameId and the guest DrawList ops, in the SAME JSON shape the JSON path emits) with its EXACT on-the-wire encoding as a lowercase hex string. The Rust encoder (crates/keel-native-guest/src/canvas_encode.rs) is the ORACLE that produces 'hex' byte-for-byte; the future TS decoder must reconstruct the frame from 'hex' — so encoder and decoder cannot silently drift together. Vectors assume a FRESH encoder per frame (intern table starts empty, indices from 0), header.flags = NONE, all scalars little-endian, all numbers f64. GENERATED by the canvas_encode.rs test (KEEL_REGEN_CANVAS_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p keel-native-guest --features binary-protocol canvas_golden_in_sync). DO NOT EDIT BY HAND.

vectors.name: font-and-color-intern
vectors.description: setFont and setFillStyle share ONE per-frame intern table: the font is index 0, the color index 1, and a repeated font reuses index 0 — mixed strings dedup together.

vectors.name: repeated-colors
vectors.description: Intern dedup: '#f00' appears in THREE ops but is stored ONCE (index 0); '#00f' is index 1. The table holds two entries, not four.

vectors.name: fill-text-multibyte
vectors.description: fillText whose text is multibyte UTF-8 ('café ☕ 日本語'): textLen is the BYTE length, greater than the char count.

vectors.name: mixed-frame
vectors.description: A realistic frame: save, style, filled backdrop, a stroked poly-line path, a text label, restore. Exercises intern reuse, inline text, path ops and the transform stack together.

vectors.name: at-limit-ops
vectors.description: An at-limit frame of exactly limits.maxOps beginPath ops — the decode-amplification boundary the host validates opCount against before its loop.
